label: 世界文学
description: アフリカ、アジア、ラテンアメリカ、中東、東欧——英語圏を超えた文学の地図。

books.title: 채식주의자
books.author: Han Kang
books.descriptionJa: ある日突然、肉を拒否し始めた平凡な主婦ヨンヘ。彼女の決断は家族を巻き込み、暴力と欲望と狂気の連鎖を引き起こす。2024年ノーベル文学賞受賞。三部構成で描かれる身体と拒絶の物語は、読む者の倫理観を静かに揺さぶる。
books.whyReadJa: ノーベル賞受賞で世界が認めた韓国文学の到達点。簡潔で詩的な文体と、身体への問いが日本文学とも深く共鳴する。隣国の現代文学を知る最良の一冊。
books.selectionReasonJa: ノーベル賞作家ハン・ガンを世界に知らしめた代表作。身体と拒絶の物語。
books.descriptionEn: One day, Yeong-hye, an ordinary housewife, decides to stop eating meat. Her quiet refusal spirals outward, entangling her family in a chain of violence, desire, and madness. Told in three parts from shifting perspectives, this novel of the body and of refusal—by the winner of the 2024 Nobel Prize in Literature—quietly unsettles everything you thought you knew about duty and freedom.
books.whyReadEn: The novel that made the world recognize Korean literature—and its Nobel-winning author. Sparse, poetic prose and a deep inquiry into the body that resonates with Japanese literature. The best single book to understand Korea's modern fiction.

books.title: Cien años de soledad
books.author: Gabriel García Márquez
books.authorJa: ガブリエル・ガルシア＝マルケス
books.descriptionJa: 架空の町マコンドを舞台に、ブエンディア一族の百年にわたる栄光と没落を描く。空を飛ぶ聖職者、何年も続く雨、処女のまま昇天する娘——日常と非日常が境界なく融合するマジックリアリズムの最高到達点。ノーベル文学賞受賞作で、世界文学の地図を塗り替えた一冊。
books.whyReadJa: 村上春樹をより深く楽しみたいなら必読。春樹文学の「異界」と現実の融合は、ここから来ている。ラテンアメリカ文学の爆発的創造力を体験できる。
books.selectionReasonJa: マジックリアリズムの最高到達点。ノーベル賞受賞の世界文学の地図を塗り替えた一冊。
books.descriptionEn: In the mythical town of Macondo, the Buendía family rises and falls across a hundred years of love, war, and solitude. A priest who levitates, a rain that lasts four years, a girl who ascends to heaven with the laundry—in Márquez's magic realism, the everyday and the miraculous flow together without a seam. The Nobel laureate's masterpiece, which redrew the map of world literature.
books.whyReadEn: Essential reading if you want to understand Murakami Haruki—the fusion of the "other world" and reality in his fiction comes from here. Experience the explosive imagination of Latin American literature at its peak.

books.author: Roberto Bolaño
books.authorJa: ロベルト・ボラーニョ
books.descriptionJa: メキシコの架空の町サンタテレサで起きる連続女性殺人事件を軸に、世界中の批評家、亡命者、狂人たちの人生が交錯する全5部構成の巨大な小説。チリ出身の作家が死の直前に完成させた「21世紀の小説」の筆頭候補。文学のすべてが詰まっていると言われる所以を体感せよ。
books.whyReadJa: 現代文学の最高到達点。ガルシア＝マルケスの後に来たラテンアメリカ文学の新たな巨人。読了後には「小説に何ができるか」の感覚が拡張されている。
books.selectionReasonJa: 現代文学の最高到達点。ボラーニョが死の直前に完成させた、21世紀の小説。
books.descriptionEn: A colossal novel in five parts, revolving around a string of unsolved murders of women in the fictional Mexican city of Santa Teresa, where the lives of critics, exiles, and madmen converge. Completed just before the Chilean author's death, 2666 is a prime candidate for the great novel of the twenty-first century—a book that seems to contain all of literature within it, from love and art to the darkest evil.
books.whyReadEn: The peak of contemporary literature, from the giant who followed García Márquez. When you finish it, your sense of what a novel can do will have been permanently expanded.

books.title: A Hora da Estrela
books.author: Clarice Lispector
books.authorJa: クラリッセ・リスペクトル
books.descriptionJa: 北東部からリオデジャネイロに出てきた貧しいタイピスト、マカベーア。彼女の「何もない」人生を、語り手が必死に言葉にしようとする。ブラジルが生んだ「最も偉大な作家」（エレーヌ・シクスー）の遺作にして最高傑作。散文そのものが哲学になる稀有な文学体験。
books.whyReadJa: 言葉が「在ること」の神秘に迫る瞬間を味わえる。村上春樹やゼーバルトのファンにも響く、内省的で詩的な語り。ブラジル文学の至宝。
books.selectionReasonJa: ブラジル文学の至宝。リスペクトルの詩的で哲学的語り。
books.descriptionEn: Macabéa, a poor typist from Brazil's northeast, lives a life of almost nothing in Rio de Janeiro. A narrator strains to put her story into words—to give her an hour of star. The final and greatest work of Clarice Lispector, called by Hélène Cixous the greatest writer Brazil has produced, it is a rare literary experience in which prose itself becomes philosophy.
books.whyReadEn: A work where language touches the mystery of being. Its introspective, poetic narration will resonate with fans of Murakami and Sebald. The jewel of Brazilian literature.

books.title: Benim Adım Kırmızı
books.author: Orhan Pamuk
books.descriptionJa: 16世紀オスマン帝国の細密画師たちの世界で起きた殺人。死体、金貨、犬、そして「赤」という色までもが語り手となる多声的ミステリ。東洋と西洋の美術の衝突、伝統と革新の葛藤を描いて、ノーベル文学賞に輝いたパムクの代表作。読むこと自体がイスタンブールを旅する体験。
books.whyReadJa: トルコ文学の最高峰。イスラム文化とヨーロッパの交差点に立つトルコは、日本が「西洋化」を考える上での鏡像でもある。知的スリラーとしても最高。
books.selectionReasonJa: 東洋と西洋の衝突を描く、ノーベル賞作家パムクの代表作。
books.descriptionEn: A murder among the miniature painters of sixteenth-century Ottoman Istanbul. Its narrators include a corpse, a gold coin, a dog—and the color red itself. As East and West collide in the art of the miniature, this polyphonic mystery—from the Nobel laureate Orhan Pamuk—becomes a meditation on tradition, innovation, and seeing. Reading it is itself a journey through Istanbul.
books.whyReadEn: The summit of Turkish literature. Turkey, at the crossroads of Islam and Europe, is a mirror for Japan's own reckoning with Westernization. Also a superb intellectual thriller.

books.title: Příliš hlučná samota
books.titleJa: あまりに騒がしい孤独
books.author: Bohumil Hrabal
books.descriptionJa: 35年間、地下の廃品処理場で紙くずをプレスし続ける老人ハンチャ。彼は捨てられた本を救い出し、読んではプレスする。その頭の中には老子からカント、ヘーゲルまでの知識が詰まっている——チェコが生んだ不条理文学の傑作。1日で読める短さの中に、文学への愛が凝縮された奇跡の一冊。
books.whyReadJa: 本を愛するすべての人に捧げられた小説。「廃品処理場の地下室で起きていること」が、これほど壮大な宇宙になりうるのかと驚かされる。カフカの後継者。
books.selectionReasonJa: 本への愛を詰め込んだ、チェコ文学の至宝。不条理の美学。
books.descriptionEn: For thirty-five years, Haňt'a has worked in a cellar compressing wastepaper into bales—but first he rescues the discarded books, reads them, and presses them, filling his head with everything from Laozi to Kant and Hegel. A miracle of a novel by the Czech master of absurdist literature: readable in a day, yet containing all the love of reading there is.
books.whyReadEn: A novel written for everyone who loves books. That a thing so small, happening in a basement baling room, can become such a vast universe is astonishing. The heir to Kafka.

books.title: 三体
books.author: Cixin Liu
books.descriptionJa: 文化大革命の中で父を失った物理学者が、宇宙人文明との接触をきっかけに人類の運命を左右する——アジア人初のヒューゴー賞を受賞したSF大作の幕開け。西洋SFとは異なる、中国文化と歴史観に根ざした宇宙文明論が新鮮。オバマ元大統領も愛読した地球規模のスケール。
books.whyReadJa: 中国が生んだ世界最大のSF。西洋中心だったSFの地図を塗り替えた記念碑的作品。科学と哲学と政治が絡み合う知的興奮。日本語訳も読みやすい。
books.selectionReasonJa: アジア初のヒューゴー賞受賞。中国SFが世界を制した記念碑的作品。
books.descriptionEn: A physicist who lost her father during the Cultural Revolution becomes the pivot on which humanity's fate turns when she makes contact with an alien civilization. This is the opening of the science fiction epic that earned Cixin Liu the first Hugo Award for an Asian author. Its vision of cosmic civilization, rooted in Chinese culture and views of history rather than in Western science fiction traditions, feels bracingly fresh. Former President Obama counted himself among its devoted readers. A story told on an Earth-spanning scale.
books.whyReadEn: The world's greatest science fiction to emerge from China, a monumental work that redrew a map once dominated by the West. It delivers the intellectual thrill of science, philosophy, and politics interwoven, and it reads smoothly in translation.

books.title: Min kamp. Første bok
books.author: Karl Ove Knausgård
books.authorJa: カール・オーヴェ・クナウスゴール
books.descriptionJa: 自分の人生をすべて書く——それ以外のルールはない。父親の死を描いた第一巻が世界を震撼させた6巻本の自伝的小説。日常の細部をこれでもかと描くことで、逆説的に「生きること」そのものを浮かび上がらせる。好き嫌いが分かれるが、ハマると他が読めなくなる。
books.whyReadJa: 「自伝」と「小説」の境界を破壊した現代文学の事件。エルノー『歳月』の男性版・超拡大版として読める。中毒性注意。
books.selectionReasonJa: 自伝と小説の境界を破壊した、現代文学の事件。
books.descriptionEn: Write everything about your life—there is no other rule. The first volume of Karl Ove Knausgård's six-book autobiographical novel, centered on his father's death, stunned readers around the world. By cataloguing the minutiae of everyday life with obsessive, relentless precision, he paradoxically brings into focus the act of living itself. Opinions divide sharply on this book, yet those who fall under its spell find it hard to read anything else afterward.
books.whyReadEn: The literary event that demolished the boundary between autobiography and fiction—a work that can be read as the male, supersized counterpart to Annie Ernaux's The Years. Beware: it is highly addictive.

books.title: Things Fall Apart
books.author: Chinua Achebe
books.descriptionJa: 植民地化以前のイボ族の社会で、尊敬を集める戦士オコンクウォの栄光と没落を描く。アフリカの側から見た「文明化」の暴力を初めて英語で語った記念碑的作品。世界中で翻訳され、アフリカ文学の古典となった。タイトルはイェイツの詩「再臨」から。
books.whyReadJa: アフリカ文学の扉を開く一冊。「西洋文学」の枠を超えて世界文学を見渡すための必読書。アチェベの視点は、戦後日本文学の「敗戦」の語り方とも響き合う。
books.selectionReasonJa: アフリカ文学の扉を開いた、植民地主義を被植民者の視点で描く原点。
books.descriptionEn: In pre-colonial Igbo society, Okonkwo, a warrior of immense renown, rises to glory only to fall. This is the monumental novel that, for the first time in English, told the story of "civilization's" violence from an African point of view. Translated throughout the world, it became the classic of African literature. The title is drawn from W.B. Yeats's poem "The Second Coming."
books.whyReadEn: The book that opens the door to African literature, essential reading for anyone who wants to see beyond the frame of "Western literature" and survey world literature whole. Achebe's perspective also resonates with the way postwar Japanese literature narrated defeat.

books.title: Midnight's Children
books.author: Salman Rushdie
books.authorJa: サルマン・ラシュディ
books.descriptionJa: 1947年8月15日——インド独立のまさにその瞬間に生まれた1,001人の子供たちは、超能力を持つ「真夜中の子供たち」だった。その一人サリーム・シンが、自分の人生とインドの歴史を重ね合わせて語るマジックリアリズムの大河。ブッカー賞受賞。
books.whyReadJa: インドという国の独立から分裂までを、一人の男の生として読む壮大な試み。マルケス『百年の孤独』の後継者として。
books.selectionReasonJa: インド独立の瞬間に生まれた超能力者たちを描く、ブッカー賞受賞の大河。
books.descriptionEn: On August 15, 1947—at the exact instant of India's independence—1,001 children are born, every one of them endowed with supernatural powers: the "midnight's children." One of them, Saleem Sinai, tells the sprawling magical-realist saga of his own life as it runs parallel to, and becomes entangled with, the history of his newborn nation. Winner of the Booker Prize.
books.whyReadEn: A grand attempt to read India's path from independence through partition and beyond as the life of a single man—the worthy successor to García Márquez's One Hundred Years of Solitude.

books.title: The God of Small Things
books.author: Arundhati Roy
books.authorJa: アルンダーティ・ロイ
books.descriptionJa: 1969年、南インドの町で起きたある「こと」——双子の兄妹と、カーストの異なる大人の男。悲劇を予感させる回想形式で、家族の秘密、カースト制度、女性の抑圧を、詩のように密度の濃い散文で描く。インドのデビュー作として史上最大のベストセラーになった。
books.whyReadJa: 英語圏文学とインドの現実が一つになった傑作。ラシュディが歴史の大きさなら、こちらは日常の細部の強度で勝負する。
books.selectionReasonJa: カーストと家族を詩的な散文で描く、ブッカー賞受賞の傑作。
books.descriptionEn: In a small town in southern India in 1969, something happens—involving twins, a brother and sister, and a grown man of a different caste. Told in flashbacks heavy with the premonition of tragedy, the novel renders family secrets, the caste system, and the oppression of women in prose as dense and lyrical as poetry. It became the best-selling debut novel in Indian publishing history.
books.whyReadEn: A masterpiece in which English-language literature and Indian reality fuse. Where Rushdie contends with the scale of history, Roy wins through the sheer intensity of everyday detail.

books.title: The Kite Runner
books.author: Khaled Hosseini
books.authorJa: カーレド・ホッセイニ
books.descriptionJa: 1970年代のカブール。富裕層の少年アミールと、その家のハザラ人使用人の息子ハッサン。凧揚げ大会を機に起きた裏切りが、二人の運命を永遠に変える。ソ連侵攻、内戦、亡命を経て、アメリカで暮らすアミールが故郷の「罪」と向き合う、世界中で読まれた物語。
books.whyReadJa: アフガニスタンの現代史を、友情と贖罪の物語として読める。ノンフィクションで見る中東情勢を、文学として体験したい人に。
books.selectionReasonJa: アフガニスタン現代史を友情と贖罪で描く、世界中で読まれた物語。
books.descriptionEn: In 1970s Kabul, Amir, a boy from a wealthy family, and Hassan, the son of the family's Hazara servant, are inseparable until a kite-fighting tournament becomes the occasion for a betrayal that changes both their fates forever. After the Soviet invasion, civil war, and exile, Amir lives in America, where he must finally confront the "sin" he left behind in his homeland. A story read all over the world.
books.whyReadEn: Afghanistan's modern history, readable as a story of friendship and redemption. For anyone who wants to experience the region's turmoil—so often met as nonfiction—in literary form.

books.title: The White Tiger
books.author: Aravind Adiga
books.authorJa: アラヴィンド・アディガ
books.descriptionJa: インドの片田舎から「起業家」に成り上がったバルラム。彼が中国の首相に向けて書く手紙の形で、カースト社会、貧困、カネと暴力のインド現代史が痛快に語られる。ブラックユーモアに満ちた反転の物語。ブッカー賞受賞。
books.whyReadJa: 『スラムドッグ$ミリオネア』的世界に、もっとシニカルな視点を足したような痛快さ。新興国の格差を笑いとともに考える。
books.selectionReasonJa: カーストと格差をブラックユーモアで描く、ブッカー賞受賞作。
books.descriptionEn: Balram rises from a village in rural India to become an "entrepreneur." In the form of a letter addressed to the Premier of China, he recounts, with relish, the modern history of India—caste society, poverty, money, and violence. A tale of reversal brimming with black humor, and a Booker Prize winner.
books.whyReadEn: The scrappiness of a Slumdog Millionaire world, sharpened with a far more cynical eye—a chance to think about inequality in the rising economies while laughing.

books.title: Half of a Yellow Sun
books.author: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
books.authorJa: チママンダ・ンゴズィ・アディーチェ
books.descriptionJa: 1960年代ナイジェリア。独立、クーデター、そして「ビアフラ戦争」。大学講師のオデニグボと、彼を愛した双子の姉妹オランナ。愛と革命と暴力が交錯する歴史小説で、アディーチェは「二つの黄色い太陽」の下で壊れていく人々を丁寧に描く。
books.whyReadJa: アフリカ現代史の悲劇を、人間の感情から描き切る力。『崩れゆく絆』のアチェベの系譜を継ぐ、現在のナイジェリア文学の頂点。
books.selectionReasonJa: ナイジェリア内戦を人間の感情から描く、現代アフリカ文学の傑作。
books.descriptionEn: In 1960s Nigeria, independence gives way to coups and then to the Biafran War. University lecturer Odenigbo and Olanna, one of the twins who loved him, are caught between love, revolution, and violence. In this historical novel Adichie follows with precision the people coming apart under "two yellow suns," rendering a national catastrophe through intimate human emotion.
books.whyReadEn: A writer who can render the tragedy of Africa's modern history entirely from human feeling. The heir to Achebe's lineage from Things Fall Apart—and the peak of contemporary Nigerian literature.

books.title: Americanah
books.author: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
books.authorJa: チママンダ・ンゴズィ・アディーチェ
books.descriptionJa: ラゴスからアメリカに留学し、人種という概念を初めて「体感」することになるイフェメル。10年後、故郷に戻った彼女が、アメリカでの経験とナイジェリアでの再出発、そして初恋の男との再会を語る。移民の目を通した人種とアイデンティティの物語。
books.whyReadJa: 「人種」を外から見るとはどういうことか——アフリカ人の目線でアメリカが描かれる。多様性論の最良の文学的回答。
books.selectionReasonJa: 移民の目線から人種を問う、現代の最重要文学の一つ。
books.descriptionEn: Ifemelu leaves Lagos to study in America, where for the first time in her life she experiences race as a lived, bodily reality. A decade later she returns home, narrating her American years, her new beginning in Nigeria, and her reunion with Obinze, her first love. A story of race and identity seen entirely through the eyes of an immigrant.
books.whyReadEn: What does it mean to see "race" from the outside? America rendered through an African gaze—arguably the best literary answer yet to debates about diversity.

books.title: Pedro Páramo
books.author: Juan Rulfo
books.descriptionJa: 亡き母の遺言で故郷コマラへ向かった青年フアン。しかしそこは死者だけが蠢く廃墟の村だった。生きているのか死んでいるのかも分からない声たちが、大地主ペドロ・パラモの話を紡いでいく。ラテンアメリカ文学の原点と言われ、マルケスやボルヘスに絶大な影響を与えた幻の傑作。
books.whyReadJa: マジックリアリズムの原型。たった120ページに、生と死、罪とメキシコの歴史が凝縮されている。
books.selectionReasonJa: マジックリアリズムの原型。死者だけが蠢く村の、ラテンアメリカ文学の原点。
books.descriptionEn: Following his dead mother's last wish, young Juan travels to her hometown of Comala—only to find a ruined village stirred by the dead. Voices that cannot be distinguished as living or dead weave together the story of the landowner Pedro Páramo. Called the origin point of Latin American literature, this legendary masterwork exerted an immense influence on García Márquez and Borges.
books.whyReadEn: The prototype of magical realism. In just 120 pages, life and death, sin, and the history of Mexico are condensed to their essence—a small book whose shadow fell over an entire continent's literature.

books.title: Crónica de una muerte anunciada
books.titleJa: 予告された殺人の記録
books.author: Gabriel García Márquez
books.authorJa: ガブリエル・ガルシア・マルケス
books.descriptionJa: サンティアゴ・ナサールが殺されると、町の誰もが前もって知っていた。なのに殺人は実行された。犯人は逮捕され、町は「予告された殺人」をなぜ止められなかったのか——事件を再構築する形で、運命と慣習と責任の網の目を描く。マルケスの最も完成度の高い作品との呼び声も高い。
books.whyReadJa: 誰もが知っていたのに止められなかった悲劇——読者もまた巻き込まれていく独特の構造。短くて文学的完成度が高い。
books.selectionReasonJa: 予告された殺人をめぐる、マルケス最も完成度の高い作品。
books.descriptionEn: Everyone in the town knew in advance that Santiago Nasar was going to be killed. And yet the murder was carried out. The killers were arrested, but why could no one stop the "foretold" crime? By reconstructing the events, Márquez traces the web of fate, custom, and responsibility. Many readers call it his most perfectly achieved novel.
books.whyReadEn: A tragedy everyone knew about yet no one managed to stop—and one whose structure drags the reader into complicity. Short, and of extraordinarily high literary finish, it may be Márquez at his most perfectly controlled.

books.title: La casa de los espíritus
books.author: Isabel Allende
books.authorJa: イサベル・アジェンデ
books.descriptionJa: 予知能力を持つ夫と、超自然的な力を持つ妻。彼らの一族トゥルエバ家の四世代にわたる物語は、チリの政治史——地主支配から社会主義、クーデター、弾圧まで——と重なり合う。ラテンアメリカを代表する女性作家アジェンデのデビュー作にして最高傑作。
books.whyReadJa: マジックリアリズムと政治史と家族のドラマの融合。マルケス好きなら必ずはまる。
books.selectionReasonJa: マジックリアリズムと政治史を融合した、チリ文学の代表作。
books.descriptionEn: A husband with the gift of precognition and a wife with supernatural powers. Their family saga, spanning four generations of the Trueba clan, runs parallel to the political history of Chile—from rule by landowners through socialism, the coup, and repression. It is the debut novel, and the masterwork, of Allende, the leading woman writer of Latin America.
books.whyReadEn: A fusion of magical realism, political history, and family drama, told across four generations. If you love García Márquez, you are all but certain to fall for this one—and to be moved by its unflinching politics.

books.title: Los detectives salvajes
books.author: Roberto Bolaño
books.authorJa: ロベルト・ボラーニョ
books.descriptionJa: 1970年代メキシコシティ。前衛詩人たちの集団「インフラレアリズム」に参加する二人の若者、アルトゥーロ・ベラーノとウリセス・リマ。彼らの遍歴を、語り手を次々に変える多声体で追う。革命、文学、青春の恍惚と喪失を描く、ボラーニョの最高傑作の一つ。
books.whyReadJa: 『2666』が巨大なら、こちらはその青春編。ラテンアメリカ文学の新しい波を体感できる。
books.selectionReasonJa: 革命と文学と青春を描く、ボラーニョの最高傑作の一つ。
books.descriptionEn: Mexico City in the 1970s: two young poets, Arturo Belano and Ulises Lima, join the avant-garde movement known as "Infrarealism." Their wanderings across countries and decades are followed through a polyphonic novel that changes narrators almost every chapter. One of Bolaño's finest works, it captures the intoxication and loss of revolution, literature, and youth.
books.whyReadEn: If 2666 is the colossal novel, this is its youth prelude—the manic, reckless younger self of Bolaño's great work. The best way to feel the new wave of Latin American literature in your hands.

books.title: El Aleph
books.author: Jorge Luis Borges
books.authorJa: ホルヘ・ルイス・ボルヘス
books.descriptionJa: 地下の一地点から全宇宙を見通せるという「アレフ」。書物と迷宮、無限と永遠をめぐるボルヘスのもう一つの短編集。『伝奇集』と並ぶ、虚構の可能性を極限まで押し広げた文学的宇宙。
books.whyReadJa: 『伝奇集』を読んだら次はこれ。ボルヘス世界をより深く堪能できる、知的な快楽の短編集。
books.selectionReasonJa: 無限と永遠をめぐる、ボルヘスのもう一つの短編集。
books.descriptionEn: The Aleph is a point beneath the floor of a Buenos Aires cellar from which the entire universe can be seen at once. This is Borges's other great collection of stories—circling books and labyrinths, the infinite and the eternal, tigers and mirrors and the branching of time. Alongside Ficciones, it forms a literary universe that pushes the possibilities of fiction to their furthest limit.
books.whyReadEn: If you have read Ficciones, this is next on the shelf. A collection of intellectual pleasures that lets you savor the Borgesian world in even greater depth—each story a compact engine of ideas.

books.title: Du côté de chez Swann
books.author: Marcel Proust
books.authorJa: マルセル・プルースト
books.descriptionJa: 「失われた時を求めて」全7巻の開幕。マドレーヌを紅茶に浸した瞬間、思い出が蘇る名場面から、語り手の幼年期、そしてスワンの恋が紡がれる。記憶と時間を主題にした20世紀文学最大の建築物の、最初の部屋。
books.whyReadJa: 「記憶の文学」の頂点。自伝的記憶を書くすべての作家（エルノー、ゼーバルト）の原点。長編への挑戦がここから始まる。
books.selectionReasonJa: 「記憶の文学」の頂点。プルースト『失われた時を求めて』の開幕。
books.descriptionEn: The opening of In Search of Lost Time, all seven volumes of it. From the famous scene in which a madeleine dipped in tea brings memories flooding back, to the narrator's childhood and Swann's great love, Proust builds the first room of the greatest edifice in twentieth-century literature—a structure devoted to memory and time.
books.whyReadEn: The summit of "literature of memory" and the origin point of every writer who has written autobiographical memory after it—Ernaux, Sebald. The long-form challenge begins here, in a novel that redefined what a novel could hold.

books.title: Der Prozess
books.author: Franz Kafka
books.descriptionJa: ある朝、銀行員ヨーゼフ・Kは何の罪も告げられぬまま逮捕される。しかし拘留はされず、いつ呼び出されるかも分からない。理不尽で不可解な裁判システムに翻弄されていくKの姿は、20世紀全体の不条理の比喩として読み継がれてきた。
books.whyReadJa: 「カフカ的」という言葉の由来になった不条理文学の原点。官僚制と権力の恐怖を文学として初めて描いた。
books.selectionReasonJa: 不条理文学の原点。官僚制と権力の恐怖を描くカフカの代表作。
books.descriptionEn: One morning, bank clerk Josef K. is arrested without being told what crime he has committed. He is not detained, and no one knows when he will be summoned. K.'s ordeal at the mercy of an absurd and unfathomable judicial system has been read ever since as a metaphor for the absurdity of the whole twentieth century.
books.whyReadEn: The origin of absurdist literature and the source of the very word "Kafkaesque." The first novel to render the terror of bureaucracy and anonymous power in purely literary form—and it has never been out of date since.

books.title: Das Schloss
books.author: Franz Kafka
books.descriptionJa: 測量士Kは城の近くの村に呼ばれたのに、城は決して彼に近づけてくれない。延々と続く官僚的迷宮への挑戦は、決して成就しない。未完成のままカフカが残したこの小説は、「到達できないものへの渇望」を最も純粋な形で描いた作品。
books.whyReadJa: 『審判』と並ぶカフカの双璧。掴めない権力の構造に立ち向かう人間の姿を、不条理の中に深い感動で描く。
books.selectionReasonJa: 到達できないものへの渇望を描く、カフカの双璧。
books.descriptionEn: Land surveyor K. has been summoned to the village near the Castle, yet the Castle never once lets him approach. His challenge against an endless bureaucratic labyrinth is never fulfilled; the novel itself was left unfinished by Kafka. What remains is the purest rendering ever written of the longing for something that can never be reached.
books.whyReadEn: Kafka's other masterpiece, the twin of The Trial. It pictures a man standing before an ungraspable structure of power, and finds within the absurd a strange and deep sympathy for its hero. Many readers find it even more moving.

books.title: Ensaio sobre a cegueira
books.author: José Saramago
books.descriptionJa: 一人の男が信号待ちの車の中で突然「白い闇」に包まれる。失明の流行病が都市を飲み込んでいく。文明が剥がれ落ちたとき、人間の尊厳はどこに残るのか——ノーベル文学賞受賞作家サラマーゴによる、恐ろしくも美しい寓話。
books.whyReadJa: パンデミックを描いた「予言の書」。人間の本質をこれほどえぐる文学は稀。ポルトガル語文学の最高峰。
books.selectionReasonJa: パンデミックを描いた「予言の書」。ノーベル賞作家サラマーゴの寓話。
books.descriptionEn: A man waiting at a traffic light is suddenly engulfed in a "white darkness." Soon an epidemic of blindness is swallowing the entire city, and society begins to come apart. When civilization peels away, where does human dignity remain? Nobel laureate Saramago's allegory is at once terrifying and beautiful, and impossible to put down.
books.whyReadEn: A "book of prophecy" written years before the pandemic—literature rarely exposes human nature so mercilessly. The highest peak of Portuguese-language fiction, and an allegory that somehow reads like a thriller.

books.title: As Intermitências da Morte
books.author: José Saramago
books.descriptionJa: ある国で、突然「死」が機能を停止した。誰も死ななくなり、国は大混乱に陥る。老女とチェリストの物語へと収束していく本書は、生と死というテーマをユーモアと哲学で紡ぐ、サラマーゴ晩年の傑作。
books.whyReadJa: 「死がなくなったら」という仮定から始まる知的遊戯。サラマーゴのウィットと深さを最も楽しめる一冊。
books.selectionReasonJa: 「死がなくなったら」を問う、サラマーゴの知的遊戯。
books.descriptionEn: In one country, death suddenly stops functioning. No one dies anymore, and the nation descends into chaos: hospitals overflow, cemeteries reach capacity, and the old and suffering are shipped to the border. Converging on the story of an old woman and a cellist, this late masterwork of Saramago weaves the great theme of life and death together with humor and philosophy.
books.whyReadEn: An intellectual game beginning from a single premise—"what if death simply ceased to exist?"—and the book that best showcases Saramago's wit and depth. Playful, sly, and unexpectedly moving.

books.title: Teoria Geral do Esquecimento
books.author: José Eduardo Agualusa
books.authorJa: ジョゼ・エドゥアルド・アグアルーザ
books.descriptionJa: 1975年、アンゴラ独立。ポルトガル人の女性ルドヴィナは、暴動から逃れるために自宅の壁に自分を封じ込め、30年間ひとりで暮らす。断絶した世界のなかで彼女が見る夢と記憶が、アンゴラという国の傷と重なる。国際IMPACダブリン文学賞受賞。
books.whyReadJa: 一人の女性の孤立が、国家の歴史になる。アフリカのポルトガル語文学の最前線を体験できる。
books.selectionReasonJa: アンゴラの独立と孤独を描く、ポルトガル語文学の傑作。
books.descriptionEn: Angola wins its independence in 1975. To escape the rioting in the streets, the Portuguese woman Ludovica walls herself up inside her own apartment and lives there alone for thirty years. The dreams and memories she sees in that severed, dreamlike world gradually overlap with the wounds of Angola itself. Winner of the International IMPAC Dublin Literary Award.
books.whyReadEn: One woman's isolation becomes the history of a nation—a haunting meditation on memory, forgetting, and what survives, and a front-row seat to the leading edge of Africa's Portuguese-language literature.

books.title: Temporada de huracanes
books.author: Fernanda Melchor
books.authorJa: フェルナンダ・メルチョール
books.descriptionJa: メキシコの田舎町の運河で、女性の死体が見つかった。「魔女」と呼ばれた彼女は何者で、なぜ殺されたのか——地元の人々の証言を集めるうちに、暴力と貧困と呪術に満ちた町の現実が浮かび上がる。世界で最も恐ろしい文章と評された、現代メキシコの暴力の鎮魂歌。
books.whyReadJa: 『2666』を継ぐ、ラテンアメリカ文学の新しい暴力の表現。強烈だが、それだけに文学の力を感じる。
books.selectionReasonJa: メキシコの暴力を描く、ラテンアメリカ文学の新しい到達点。
books.descriptionEn: A woman's body is found in a canal in a rural Mexican town. Who was this woman called "the witch," and why was she killed? As the testimony of local people accumulates, the reality of a town steeped in violence, poverty, and sorcery rises to the surface. Hailed as some of the most terrifying prose in the world, this is a requiem for the violence of modern Mexico.
books.whyReadEn: The new language of violence in Latin American literature, carrying 2666 into the present. Fierce, unrelenting, and at times nearly unbearable—and all the more powerful for it. Melchor is the real thing.

books.title: The Tenth Muse
books.author: Catherine Chung
books.descriptionJa: 数学に才能を捧げた女性カスリーヌ。第二次世界大戦、秘密の暗号解読、そして彼女を追いかける謎の数学者——数学と歴史とアイデンティティが交差する、知性のサスペンス。女性数学者の実在をめぐる「沈黙の歴史」への問いかけ。
books.whyReadJa: 「数学の証明は美しい」と信じるすべての人に。ミステリと歴史小説と成長物語が一つになった稀有な作品。
books.selectionReasonJa: 女性数学者の沈黙の歴史を描く、知性のサスペンス。
books.descriptionEn: Katherine devotes her extraordinary gift to mathematics, the one place where she feels free. But World War II, secret code-breaking, and a mysterious mathematician who follows her through history turn her life into an intellectual suspense story in which mathematics, history, and identity converge. It is also a question aimed at the "silent history" of the real women mathematicians erased from the record.
books.whyReadEn: For everyone who believes that a mathematical proof can be beautiful. A rare work that fuses mystery, historical novel, and coming-of-age story into one—and one that honors the women mathematics forgot.

books.title: The Shape of the Ruins
books.author: Juan Gabriel Vásquez
books.authorJa: フアン・ガブリエル・バスケス
books.descriptionJa: 1991年、コロンビアの政治家が暗殺された。その事件の「陰謀」を追う男に魅せられた語り手は、コロンビアの隠された歴史の層を掘り下げていく。事実と陰謀論の境界で揺れる、政治的記憶の探求の物語。
books.whyReadJa: 真実の探求が次第に狂気へ変わる過程が秀逸。ラテンアメリカ政治史を文学として体験したい人に。
books.selectionReasonJa: 真実の探求が狂気へ変わる、コロンビア政治史の文学。
books.descriptionEn: In 1991, a Colombian politician is assassinated. The narrator, fascinated by a man who devotes his life to pursuing the "conspiracy" behind the killing, digs down through the hidden layers of Colombia's history—its forgotten crimes and buried traumas. A story of political memory that sways perpetually on the boundary between fact and conspiracy theory.
books.whyReadEn: The process by which the pursuit of truth slides, degree by degree, into obsession is rendered masterfully. For anyone who wants to experience Latin American political history as literature—this is a doorway.

books.title: The Namesake
books.author: Jhumpa Lahiri
books.descriptionJa: ベンガル系移民の息子ゴーゴルは、父が命名した「ゴーゴリ」という名前の重さとともに、アメリカでアイデンティティを模索する。移民と世代、名前と自己をめぐる、ラヒリの代表作。
books.whyReadJa: 「名前」を通して移民のアイデンティティを描く傑作。ディアスポラ文学の繊細な到達点。
books.selectionReasonJa: 名前を通して移民のアイデンティティを描く、ラヒリの代表作。
books.descriptionEn: Gogol, the son of Bengali immigrants, grows up in America carrying the weight of the name his father chose for him—"Gogol," after the Russian writer. Through that name he searches, across two generations and two cultures, for an identity that belongs to him. Jhumpa Lahiri's representative novel is about immigration and family, names and the self.
books.whyReadEn: A masterpiece that portrays immigrant identity through the prism of a name—the delicate, exacting summit of diaspora literature, and the book that made Lahiri a household name among readers of world fiction.

books.title: The Lowland
books.author: Jhumpa Lahiri
books.descriptionJa: コルカタの低地に育った兄弟。兄は政治運動に身を投じ、弟はアメリカで科学者になる。ナクサル運動というインドの歴史が、家族の運命をどう分けたのか。ブッカー賞候補、ラヒリの大河小説。
books.whyReadJa: 個人の選択と歴史の暴力。インド現代史と移民の物語を、抑制された筆致で描く。
books.selectionReasonJa: インド現代史と移民を抑制された筆致で描く、ラヒリの大河。
books.descriptionEn: Two brothers grow up together on the marshy lowlands of Kolkata, inseparable until adulthood. The elder throws himself into the Naxalite movement; the younger becomes a scientist in America and marries the woman his brother loved. How does the violence of India's modern history divide the fate of one family? A Booker Prize finalist and Lahiri's great family saga.
books.whyReadEn: Individual choice set against the violence of history. India's modern history and the immigrant's story are written here in a restrained hand, in prose that grows more devastating the quieter it becomes.

books.title: Interpreter of Maladies
books.author: Jhumpa Lahiri
books.descriptionJa: ボストンとコルカタ、二つの世界に生きる人々の日常を描く短編集。ピューリッツァー賞を受賞し、ラヒリの名を世界に知らしめたデビュー作。抑制された文体の中に、移民の孤独と希望が滲む。
books.whyReadJa: 短編文学の傑作。ラヒリの世界へ入るのに最適な一冊。
books.selectionReasonJa: ピューリッツァー賞受賞。ラヒリの移民の孤独と希望の短編集。
books.descriptionEn: Nine short stories of people living between two worlds—Boston and Kolkata, the arranged and the chosen, the familiar and the strange. This debut collection won the Pulitzer Prize and made Lahiri's name known throughout the world. Within its restrained, immaculate style, the loneliness and hope of immigrants seep through every sentence.
books.whyReadEn: A masterpiece of the short story, in which every piece is a small perfect engine of feeling. The best single volume for entering Lahiri's world—and the reason she is now read everywhere.

books.title: Persepolis
books.author: Marjane Satrapi
books.authorJa: マルジャン・サトラピ
books.descriptionJa: イラン革命と戦争の只中で少女が成長する自伝的グラフィックノベル。ヒジャブ、検閲、拷問、そして自由への憧れ——抑圧の社会で自己を保つことの難しさを、ユーモアと痛みで描く。
books.whyReadJa: 中東の現代史を、ひとりの少女の目から知ることができる名作。映画化もされた。
books.selectionReasonJa: イラン革命を少女の目から描く、自伝的グラフィックノベル。
books.descriptionEn: An autobiographical graphic novel in which a girl grows up in Tehran through the Iranian Revolution and the war with Iraq. The hijab, censorship, torture, and a fierce longing for freedom—the difficulty of keeping a self alive in an oppressive society, rendered with humor and pain in stark black-and-white.
books.whyReadEn: A classic that lets you meet the modern history of the Middle East through the eyes of one sharp-tongued, unforgettable girl. It was made into an animated film, but the book is the deeper pleasure.

books.title: A Thousand Splendid Suns
books.author: Khaled Hosseini
books.authorJa: カーレド・ホッセイニ
books.descriptionJa: アフガニスタンで、年齢の違う二人の女性マリアムとライラが、同じ夫の妻として繋がれながらも、互いに支え合い生きていく。タリバン支配下のカブールで女性が生きることの意味を問う、世界中で読まれた感動作。
books.whyReadJa: 『カイト・ランナー』の作者による、女性たちの物語。アフガニスタンの現代史を人間の視点から。
books.selectionReasonJa: タリバン下のカブールで女性が生きることを問う、ホッセイニの感動作。
books.descriptionEn: In Afghanistan, two women of different generations—Mariam, the illegitimate daughter of a wealthy man, and Laila, a girl of the same house—are bound together as wives of the same man, and yet they come to support each other and survive. A deeply moving novel read around the world, it asks what it means for a woman to live under Taliban rule in Kabul.
books.whyReadEn: The author of The Kite Runner turns his attention to the women of Afghanistan. The country's modern history, told from a deeply human vantage point—harrowing, tender, and impossible to forget. Many readers find it even more powerful than his first novel.

books.title: Mémoires d'Hadrien
books.titleJa: ハドリアヌス帝の回想
books.author: Marguerite Yourcenar
books.authorJa: マルグリット・ユルスナール
books.descriptionJa: ローマ皇帝ハドリアヌスが、死を目前に遺した「手紙」という形式の傑作。権力、芸術、愛、そして死——古代世界の人物が、近代の眼で描かれる。フランス文学史上最高の歴史小説の一つ。
books.whyReadJa: 歴史小説の到達点。過去の人物を「生きた人間」として蘇らせる、言葉の力に圧倒される。
books.selectionReasonJa: フランス文学史上最高の歴史小説。ローマ皇帝を生きた人間として蘇らせる。
books.descriptionEn: A masterpiece in the form of a "letter" that the Roman emperor Hadrian addresses to his successor on the eve of his death. Power, art, love, and death—an ancient figure of the world is reimagined through a modern, knowing eye, and a life becomes a meditation on everything that matters. One of the greatest historical novels in the history of French literature.
books.whyReadEn: The summit of the historical novel. The power of language to resurrect a figure of the past as a living, breathing human being is overwhelming—this is the book that made Marguerite Yourcenar the first woman in the Académie française.

books.title: Смерть Ивана Ильича
books.titleJa: イワン・イリイチの死
books.author: Leo Tolstoy
books.descriptionJa: 完璧な人生を送ってきたはずの裁判官イワン・イリイチが、突然の病で死に向き合う。自分の人生は「まちがいだった」——死の寸前で彼が見るものとは。人間の生の虚実を問う、トルストイの傑作中編。
books.whyReadJa: 「死」をめぐる文学の最高傑作の一つ。短いが、生き方を根底から問い直させる。
books.selectionReasonJa: 「死」をめぐる文学の最高傑作。短いが、生き方を根底から問い直す。
books.descriptionEn: Judge Ivan Ilyich has led what should have been a perfect life—a good career, a fine marriage, a house, respectability—until a sudden illness forces him to face death. "My life was a mistake." What does he see in the final moments before death? A masterpiece novella in which Tolstoy interrogates the truth and falsehood of an ordinary human life.
books.whyReadEn: One of the greatest works of literature ever written about death. Short enough to read in an evening, yet it will force you to reexamine the very foundations of how you live.

books.title: Крейцерова соната
books.titleJa: クロイツェル・ソナタ
books.author: Leo Tolstoy
books.descriptionJa: 妻を殺した男の告白。嫉妬、結婚、性——トルストイが最も激しく問うた、愛と所有の病理。ロシア文学のタブーに切り込んだ、衝撃の一冊。
books.whyReadJa: 「愛と嫉妬」をこれほど赤裸々に描いた小説は稀。トルストイの深層に触れる。
books.selectionReasonJa: 愛と嫉妬の病理を赤裸々に描く、トルストイの衝撃作。
books.descriptionEn: The confession of a man who murdered his wife, told to a stranger on a train. Jealousy, marriage, sex—the pathology of love and possession that Tolstoy interrogated most fiercely, drawing on the dark corners of his own marriage. A shocking book that cut into the taboos of Russian literature, and still scandalous today.
books.whyReadEn: A novel that exposes "love and jealousy" so nakedly is rare in any literature. Here you touch the deepest, most unsettled layers of Tolstoy—and are made to think about possession in love long after the last page.

books.title: The Shadow of the Wind
books.author: Carlos Ruiz Zafón
books.authorJa: カルロス・ルイス・サフォン
books.descriptionJa: バルセロンの「忘れられた本の墓地」で、少年ダニエルは一冊の本と出会う。『風の影』を書いた作家を探すうちに、彼は書物と死と愛をめぐる迷宮に足を踏み入れる。世界中で4000万部超のベストセラー。
books.whyReadJa: 「本」をめぐる物語の金字塔。書物と運命が絡み合う、魅惑的な文学ミステリ。
books.selectionReasonJa: 「忘れられた本の墓地」から始まる、書物と運命をめぐる世界中で4000万部超のベストセラー。
books.descriptionEn: In the "Cemetery of Forgotten Books" in Barcelona, the boy Daniel is allowed to adopt a single volume—The Shadow of the Wind. As he searches for its mysterious author, he steps into a labyrinth of books, death, and love that reaches back through his city's history. A bestseller with more than 40 million copies sold worldwide, and the opening of a legendary cycle.
books.whyReadEn: The landmark story about "books" themselves—a bewitching literary mystery in which books and fate, readers and secrets are entwined. The perfect gateway into one of modern publishing's most beloved series.

books.title: El laberinto de los espíritus
books.author: Carlos Ruiz Zafón
books.authorJa: カルロス・ルイス・サフォン
books.descriptionJa: 「風の影」四部作の最終章。独裁体制下のバルセロナで、書店員の娘アリシアが失踪事件の謎を追う。書物、記憶、そしてスペイン内戦の影——サフォンの物語世界が集大成に達する。
books.whyReadJa: 『風の影』の世界を完結させる、書物をめぐる大河の到達点。
books.selectionReasonJa: 「風の影」四部作の最終章。独裁体制下のバルセロナを書物と記憶で描く、サフォンの物語世界の集大成。
books.descriptionEn: The final volume of the four-part cycle that began with The Shadow of the Wind. In Barcelona under the Franco dictatorship, Alicia, the bookseller's daughter, pursues the mystery of a disappearance that leads into the darkest corners of the regime. Books, memory, and the shadow of the Spanish Civil War—Zafón's narrative world reaches its full culmination here.
books.whyReadEn: The culmination of the great saga about books—the volume in which the world of The Shadow of the Wind closes its circle. For anyone who has followed Daniel and Fermín, an essential and deeply satisfying conclusion.

books.title: The Sandcastle
books.author: Iris Murdoch
books.authorJa: アイリス・マードック
books.descriptionJa: 堅実な家庭を持つ中年の古典教師モーは、画家志望の若い女性に惹かれる。選択と欲望、義務と自由——マードックが初期に描いた、人間の恋愛の諸相。
books.whyReadJa: 道徳と欲望の葛藤を描く、マードック文学の入門。
books.selectionReasonJa: 選択と欲望を描く、マードック文学の入門。
books.descriptionEn: Mor, a middle-aged classics teacher with a stable family and a secure career, is drawn to a young woman who dreams of becoming a painter. As he hesitates between them, choice and desire, duty and freedom pull him in different directions—the facets of human love that Iris Murdoch mapped out in her early work.
books.whyReadEn: A lucid introduction to Murdoch's fiction—a study of the conflict between morality and desire, written with the philosophical seriousness that would define her entire career. The ideal starting point for her world.

books.title: The Black Prince
books.author: Iris Murdoch
books.authorJa: アイリス・マードック
books.descriptionJa: 売れない作家ブラッドリーは、友人の妻に恋をする。語りは章ごとに別の人物によって覆され、真実が揺らぐ。マードックの最高傑作の一つで、芸術と愛の関係をめぐる哲学的傑作。
books.whyReadJa: 「語り」の信頼性を揺さぶる構成が秀逸。芸術と欲望を哲学する。
books.selectionReasonJa: 語りの信頼性を揺さぶる、マードックの哲学的傑作。
books.descriptionEn: Bradley Pearson, a struggling, middle-aged writer, falls in love with the wife of his friend—and catastrophe follows. Narrated across chapters that each overturn what came before, the story's "truth" begins to waver, and the reader is left to judge. One of Murdoch's finest works, and a philosophical masterpiece on the relation between art and love.
books.whyReadEn: A masterly structure that shakes your trust in the narration itself—each section rewrites the last. Philosophy of art and desire in one volume, and one of the most intellectually exciting novels of the twentieth century.

books.title: The Sea, the Sea
books.author: Iris Murdoch
books.authorJa: アイリス・マードック
books.descriptionJa: 舞台から引退した演出家チャールズは、海辺の村で静かに暮らそうとするが、初恋の女性と再会し、妄想と執着の物語が始まる。ブッカー賞受賞。自己欺瞞を描く文学の極致。
books.whyReadJa: 「自分を騙す」人間の滑稽さと哀しみ。マードック最高傑作。
books.selectionReasonJa: 自己欺瞞を描く、ブッカー賞受賞のマードック最高傑作。
books.descriptionEn: Charles Arrowby, a celebrated theater director, retires from the stage to a remote seaside village, hoping for a quiet life. Instead he reunites with his first love and a story of delusion, obsession, and self-justification begins. Winner of the Booker Prize, it is arguably literature's most extreme case study in self-deception.
books.whyReadEn: The comedy and the sorrow of human beings who deceive themselves—rendered by Murdoch at the height of her powers. It won the Booker Prize and remains her masterpiece: layered, funny, and quietly devastating.

books.title: Nesnesitelná lehkost bytí
books.titleJa: 存在の耐えられない軽さ
books.author: Milan Kundera
books.descriptionJa: 「一度しか生きられないのなら、人生は何の重みもない」。プラハの春の時代を生きた男女の愛と政治をめぐる、クンデラの代表作。軽さと重さ、個と社会を哲学的に織り込む。
books.whyReadJa: 「一回性の人生」という問い。哲学と小説が融合した、20世紀文学の頂点の一つ。
books.selectionReasonJa: 「一回性の人生」を問う、哲学と小説が融合した20世紀文学の頂点。
books.descriptionEn: If you live only once, your life has no weight. Set against the Prague Spring and its aftermath, this is Kundera's representative novel about the love, politics, and choices of Tomáš, Tereza, and Sabina. Lightness and weight, the individual and society, the eternal return and its absence—all are woven together with philosophy.
books.whyReadEn: The question of a "one-time life"—if nothing repeats, what does anything weigh? Philosophy and fiction fused into a novel among the summits of twentieth-century literature, and one that stays with you for decades.

books.title: Kniha smíchu a zapomnění
books.author: Milan Kundera
books.descriptionJa: 忘却と記憶、笑いと笑いの暴力。チェコの共産主義体制下の歴史を断片として織り込みながら、七つの物語が交錯する。クンデラの手法が最も冴える傑作。
books.whyReadJa: 「記憶」をテーマにした文学の到達点。ゼーバルトやエルノーにも通じる。
books.selectionReasonJa: 記憶と忘却を断片で描く、クンデラの手法が冴える傑作。
books.titleEn: The Book of Laughter and Forgetting
books.descriptionEn: Forgetting and memory, laughter and the violence of laughter. Seven interlocking stories weave in fragments of Czech history under the communist regime—erasures, purges, and the way power seizes the past. It is Kundera's most brilliant performance as a novelist, and one of the essential works of the Cold War canon.
books.whyReadEn: A summit of literature devoted to "memory"—how nations and individuals forget, and what that forgetting costs. It connects directly to the great memory-writers Sebald and Ernaux, and is as urgent now as ever.

books.title: The White Goddess
books.author: Robert Graves
books.authorJa: ロバート・グレーヴス
books.descriptionJa: 詩の源泉には「白い女神」という原初の女神がいる——神話、詩、言語を横断して、詩の本質を探るグレーヴスの問題作。神話研究と詩論が融合した、文学の隠れた古典。
books.whyReadJa: 神話と文学の関係を深く知りたい人に。詩作の神秘を言語学的に解き明かす。
books.selectionReasonJa: 詩の本質を言語学的に解き明かす、グレーヴズの神話学。
books.descriptionEn: At the source of poetry, Graves argues, stands a primordial goddess—the White Goddess, to whom poets have secretly addressed their verse for millennia. Crossing myth, poetry, and language, this provocative work probes the very essence of poetic creation. A hidden classic in which mythology and literary theory fuse into a single, dazzling argument.
books.whyReadEn: For anyone who wants to understand the deep relation between myth and literature—an unravelling of the mystery of poetic creation through myth, linguistics, and learning. Dense, eccentric, and endlessly suggestive.

books.title: The Crow Road
books.author: Iain Banks
books.descriptionJa: スコットランドの一族の物語。ユーモア、家族、死と秘密が織りなす、現代イギリス文学の傑作。語り手の思い出話の冒頭「母は事故で死んだのではなく、殺されたのだ」から始まる。
books.whyReadJa: スコットランド文学の最良の入り口。家族と秘密とユーモアの物語。
books.selectionReasonJa: スコットランド文学の最良の入口。家族と秘密とユーモア。
books.descriptionEn: The story of a Scottish family, told across generations and through the memories of the young narrator. Humor, family, death, and secrets are interwoven in a masterpiece of contemporary British literature. It opens with the narrator's remembered words: "My mother did not die in an accident—she was killed." Few novels balance wit and grief so well.
books.whyReadEn: The finest gateway into Scottish literature—a story of family, secrets, and humor that opens with one of the most arresting first lines in modern fiction. Banks balances wit and grief with extraordinary grace.

books.title: Complicity
books.author: Iain Banks
books.descriptionJa: 新聞記者キャメロンに、連続殺人の謎の「共犯者」から連絡が来る。彼は事件について何を知っているのか——Banksの犯罪小説で最も鋭い一冊。社会の不正義への怒りが、物語の原動力となる。
books.whyReadJa: 社会批判とサスペンスを融合した、バンクスの代表作。
books.selectionReasonJa: 社会批判とサスペンスを融合した、バンクスの代表作。
books.descriptionEn: Cameron, a newspaper journalist, begins to receive contact from the mysterious "accomplice" behind a series of brutal murders. Each killing is somehow linked to his own investigations. What does he really know about the crimes—and how much is he responsible for? The sharpest of Iain Banks's crime novels, driven by genuine rage at society's injustices.
books.whyReadEn: Banks at his most ferocious—social critique and suspense fused into a single, propulsive engine. A thriller with a conscience, and one of the most morally angry crime novels of its decade.

books.title: The Spiral Staircase
books.author: Karen Armstrong
books.authorJa: カレン・アームストロング
books.descriptionJa: 修道院を飛び出した元修道女が、学者として再生するまでの回想録。信仰と不信、知と魂の葛藤を、率直に描く。宗教と現代社会をめぐる傑作ノンフィクション。
books.whyReadJa: 「信仰を失った人」が信仰について考える、知性の旅。
books.selectionReasonJa: 修道院を飛び出した元修道女が学者になる、宗教と知の回想録。
books.descriptionEn: The memoir of a former nun who fled her convent—and, with it, a faith she could no longer hold—only to be reborn as a scholar of religion. With rare candor, Karen Armstrong recounts the struggle between faith and doubt, knowledge and the soul, across decades of her own life. A masterwork of nonfiction on religion and modern society.
books.whyReadEn: An intellectual journey in which a person who lost faith sets out to think honestly about faith itself. Honest, learned, and moving—a model of how to examine the deepest questions without flinching.

books.title: The Marriage Plot
books.author: Jeffrey Eugenides
books.authorJa: ジェフリー・ユージェニデス
books.descriptionJa: 1980年代、ブラウン大学。文学を学ぶ三人の若者——マドレーヌ、レナード、ミッチェル。愛と躁鬱と文学理論のあいだを揺れる青春を描く、ユージェニデスの現代的な恋愛小説。
books.whyReadJa: 「文学と人生」をめぐる教養小説。知的で、どこか切ない。
books.selectionReasonJa: 「文学と人生」をめぐる、ユージェニデスの教養小説。
books.descriptionEn: Brown University in the 1980s. Three young people studying literature—Madeleine, devoted to the Victorian marriage plot; Leonard, brilliant and burdened by manic depression; and Mitchell, seeking meaning in religion—are caught in a triangle of love and ideas. A contemporary love story in which Eugenides renders their youth with intelligence and wistfulness.
books.whyReadEn: A bildungsroman about literature and life—intellectual, warm, and somehow wistful. For anyone who has wondered whether love can be explained by literary theory, or survived the Great Books seminar intact.

books.title: The Virgin Suicides
books.titleJa: ヴァージン・スーサイズ
books.author: Jeffrey Eugenides
books.authorJa: ジェフリー・ユージェニデス
books.descriptionJa: 1970年代のデトロイト郊外。五人のリスボン姉妹が相次いで自殺した。近所の少年たちは、彼女たちの謎を一生かけて追い続ける。映画化もされた、ユージェニデスのデビュー作。
books.whyReadJa: 「少女たちの謎」をめぐる、詩的で美しい青春小説。
books.selectionReasonJa: 五人の姉妹の謎をめぐる、ユージェニデスの詩的な青春小説。
books.descriptionEn: In a leafy suburb of Detroit in the 1970s, the five Lisbon sisters—ages thirteen to seventeen—kill themselves, one after another, over a single year. The boys who lived next door spend the rest of their lives trying to understand these girls and the mystery of their deaths. Eugenides's haunting debut novel, made into an acclaimed film by Sofia Coppola.
books.whyReadEn: A poetic, beautiful novel of youth that circles "the mystery of the girls" without ever quite solving it—and is the wiser for it. One of the most distinctive debut novels in recent American fiction.

books.title: The Thing Around Your Neck
books.titleJa: あなたの首のまわりに
books.author: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
books.authorJa: チママンダ・ンゴズィ・アディーチェ
books.descriptionJa: ナイジェリアとアメリカを往復する人々の十二篇。移民の孤独、差別、そして故郷への想いを、鋭く繊細に描く短編集。アディーチェの世界観を一冊で味わえる。
books.whyReadJa: 移民の「見えない境界」を描く、現代短編の秀作。
books.selectionReasonJa: 移民の「見えない境界」を描く、アディーチェの短編秀作。
books.descriptionEn: Twelve stories of people moving between Nigeria and America—students, refugees, professors, waitresses—who carry a homeland with them and feel its weight around their necks. With sharpness and delicacy, Adichie renders the loneliness of immigrants, the sting of everyday discrimination, and the pull of home. A single volume in which her entire worldview can be tasted.
books.whyReadEn: A fine collection of contemporary short fiction about the "invisible borders" immigrants cross every day. Adichie at full power in miniature—a perfect introduction to her sensibility, and a book that rewards rereading.

books.title: The Great Divorce
books.author: C.S. Lewis
books.descriptionJa: 地獄から天国へのバス旅行——死者たちが自由意志で天国へ向かうとき、彼らが抱えている「小さなこだわり」とは。ルイスによる、自由と選択をめぐる寓話。キリスト教的ファンタジーの古典。
books.whyReadJa: 「なぜ人は幸せを拒むのか」を描く、静かな寓話。宗教哲学と文学の融合。
books.selectionReasonJa: 自由と選択をめぐる、ルイスのキリスト教的寓話。
books.descriptionEn: A bus trip from Hell to Heaven. The dead are offered a chance to board, and those who go find Heaven strange—too bright, too hard, too demanding. What small attachments keep each soul from staying? C.S. Lewis's allegory of freedom and choice is a classic of Christian fantasy, and a quietly devastating answer to the question of why people refuse happiness.
books.whyReadEn: A quiet allegory about "why people refuse happiness"—where religious philosophy and literature meet and illuminate each other. Short, strange, and unforgettable; it will make you reconsider your own small attachments.

books.title: Prince Caspian
books.titleJa: カスピアン王子の角笛
books.author: C.S. Lewis
books.descriptionJa: ナルニア国の王子カスピアン。叔父に王位を奪われ、森へ逃げた彼は、古の生き物たちとともに反乱を起こす。「ナルニア国物語」シリーズ第二作。
books.whyReadJa: ナルニアシリーズを続けて読むなら。成長と正義の物語。
books.selectionReasonJa: ナルニアシリーズ第二作。成長と正義の物語。
books.descriptionEn: Prince Caspian of Narnia, robbed of his throne by his scheming uncle, flees into the forest and raises a rebellion together with the ancient creatures of the land—talking animals, dwarfs, and centaurs. When the Pevensie children return to Narnia, they join the fight to restore what was taken. The second book of the Chronicles of Narnia.
books.whyReadEn: For continuing the Narnia series—a story of growth, courage, and the restoration of justice. Lewis's imagination at its most vivid: wise, adventurous, and warm—and a deeper meditation on belief than it first appears.

books.title: The Voyage of the Dawn Treader
books.author: C.S. Lewis
books.descriptionJa: 世界の果てを目指す船、朝びらき丸。ルーシーとエドマンド、そしてカスピアンが海図にない島々を巡る。「ナルニア国物語」第三作。
books.whyReadJa: 「世界の果て」への航海。ファンタジーの冒険譚として最も美しい。
books.selectionReasonJa: ナルニア第三作。世界の果てへの航海の美しい冒険譚。
books.titleEn: The Voyage of the Dawn Treader
books.descriptionEn: A ship bound for the end of the world: the Dawn Treader, carrying Lucy, Edmund, their difficult cousin Eustace, and Caspian on a voyage among islands that appear on no map. They meet dragons, sea serpents, and the very edge of the world itself. The third book of the Chronicles of Narnia, and the purest adventure in the series.
books.whyReadEn: A voyage to "the end of the world"—the most beautiful adventure tale in fantasy. Lewis writes here with the lyricism and strangeness that made the Narnia books beloved across generations and continents.

books.title: The Tin Drum
books.author: Günter Grass
books.descriptionJa: 三歳で「成長をやめる」ことを決めたオスカルが、ブリキの太鼓を叩き、ガラスを割る声で世界に復讐する。ドイツ戦後文学の最高傑作にしてノーベル文学賞受賞作。20世紀の悪夢を寓話として描く。
books.whyReadJa: ドイツの戦後史を、最も過激で豊かな想像力で描いた書。『百年の孤独』と並ぶ20世紀小説。
books.selectionReasonJa: ドイツ戦後文学の最高傑作。20世紀の悪夢を寓話として描くノーベル賞作。
books.descriptionEn: At age three, Oskar Matzerath decides to stop growing—and takes revenge on the world, beating his tin drum and shattering glass with a scream that can cut through walls. Set against the rise of Nazism and the war, Günter Grass's Nobel Prize–winning novel is the supreme masterwork of postwar German literature, rendering the nightmare of the twentieth century as grotesque, hilarious allegory.
books.whyReadEn: Postwar Germany's history, written with the most radical and abundant imagination of its age. A twentieth-century novel that stands beside One Hundred Years of Solitude—and one of the strangest, most unforgettable reading experiences in modern fiction.

books.title: The Go-Between
books.author: L.P. Hartley
books.descriptionJa: 1900年の夏、貴族の屋敷に滞在した少年レオは、姉の恋人と隣家の娘の「仲介人」を務める。一夏の秘密が、彼の一生を決定づける。「過去は外国であり、彼らはそこで違ったことをする」。
books.whyReadJa: イギリス文学の名作。ノスタルジーと喪失を、繊細な記憶の語りで描く。
books.selectionReasonJa: 一夏の秘密が一生を決める、イギリス文学の記憶の名作。
books.descriptionEn: In the summer of 1900, Leo Colston, a thirteen-year-old boy, stays at a great aristocratic house and becomes the unwitting go-between for his older friend's fiancé and the girl from the neighboring family. One summer's secret decides the course of his entire life. "The past is a foreign country: they do things differently there." A classic of English literature.
books.whyReadEn: A classic of English literature—nostalgia and loss rendered through a delicate narration of memory, and a devastating portrait of childhood innocence destroyed. Its famous first line has entered the language, and its last page is unforgettable.

books.title: The Painted Veil
books.author: W. Somerset Maugham
books.authorJa: W・サマセット・モーム
books.descriptionJa: 軽薄な女性キティは、夫に連れられ中国のコレラ流行地へ行く。死と向き合う中で、彼女は人生の意味を見いだしていく。モームの代表作の一つで、愛と償いを描く古典。
books.whyReadJa: 「結婚と自己欺瞞」を描く、モームの名作。短くて完成度が高い。
books.selectionReasonJa: 愛と償いを描く、モームの古典的名作。
books.descriptionEn: Kitty, a beautiful and frivolous young woman, marries for the wrong reasons and is then taken by her bacteriologist husband to a cholera-ravaged region of China as punishment for her affair. Facing death and illness among strangers, she slowly discovers meaning in her own life. One of Maugham's representative novels—a classic of love, betrayal, and atonement.
books.whyReadEn: Maugham's masterwork on "marriage and self-deception," told with his characteristic economy and irony. Short, and highly finished—a perfect place to begin with one of the most widely read novelists of the twentieth century.

books.title: The Moon and Sixpence
books.author: W. Somerset Maugham
books.authorJa: W・サマセット・モーム
books.descriptionJa: 優雅な生活を捨て、パリからタヒチへ——伝説の画家ゴーギャンをモデルに、アートのための人生を選んだ男を描く。芸術と世俗の対立をめぐる、モームの最も有名な小説。
books.whyReadJa: 「芸術のためなら何を捨てられるか」。画家と作家の違いを描く古典。
books.selectionReasonJa: 芸術のための人生を問う、モームの最も有名な小説。
books.descriptionEn: A respectable London stockbroker walks away from his wife, his children, and his comfortable life to become a painter—first in Paris, then on the islands of Tahiti. Modeled on the legendary artist Gauguin, the book is a portrait of a man who chooses a life devoted entirely to art. Maugham's most famous novel, on the conflict between art and the world.
books.whyReadEn: What are you willing to give up for art? A classic that draws a stark line between the artist and the respectable citizen, and asks which life is truly lived. Maugham at his most provocative, and his most quotable.

books.title: The Man Who Was Thursday
books.author: G.K. Chesterton
books.descriptionJa: 無政府主義者の秘密結社に潜入した警官シンメ。しかし組織のメンバーは次々と正体を明かしていく——「実は私も警官だ」。イリュージョンと逆転を重ねる、チェスタトンの奇想天外な傑作。
books.whyReadJa: 哲学とミステリとユーモアの融合。ボルヘスも愛した古典。
books.selectionReasonJa: イリュージョンと逆転を重ねる、チェスタトンの奇想天外な傑作。
books.descriptionEn: Poet and police detective Gabriel Syme infiltrates an anarchist secret society. But one by one, its seven members reveal themselves—each is, in fact, a policeman. Layer after layer of illusion and reversal unfolds until the chase leads to a breathtaking, philosophical conclusion. A wildly inventive masterpiece from G.K. Chesterton, beloved by Borges.
books.whyReadEn: Philosophy, mystery, and humor fused into a single astonishing contraption—a classic that Borges himself loved. No one builds an argument inside a chase quite like Chesterton, and this is his most exhilarating.

books.title: The Heart Is a Lonely Hunter
books.author: Carson McCullers
books.authorJa: カーソン・マッカラーズ
books.descriptionJa: 南部の小さな町。聾唖者のジョン・シンガーを中心に、五人の孤独な人々が彼に心の内を打ち明ける。孤独と連帯をめぐる、マッカラーズのデビュー作にして代表作。
books.whyReadJa: 「孤独」をめぐるアメリカ文学の古典。聾唖者に語る人々の、切ない共鳴。
books.selectionReasonJa: 孤独をめぐるアメリカ文学の古典。マッカラーズの代表作。
books.titleEn: The Heart Is a Lonely Hunter
books.descriptionEn: In a small Southern mill town, five lonely people—a young girl, a drifter, a black doctor, and a cafe owner—each confide the contents of their hearts to John Singer, a gentle deaf-mute. In his silence they find the only listener who truly hears them. Carson McCullers's debut novel, and still her most loved work, on loneliness and the longing for connection.
books.whyReadEn: A classic of American literature about loneliness—the poignant resonance of people pouring out their hearts to a deaf-mute who cannot answer. McCullers wrote it at twenty-three, and it has never lost its power.

books.title: The Member of the Wedding
books.author: Carson McCullers
books.authorJa: カーソン・マッカラーズ
books.descriptionJa: 十二歳のフランキーは、兄の結婚式に「同行する」ことに固執する。青春期の孤独と、誰かと一つになりたいという願いを描く。マッカラーズの最も愛される作品。
books.whyReadJa: 思春期の感覚をこれほど正確に描ける作家はいない。短くて美しい。
books.selectionReasonJa: 思春期の孤独と願いを描く、マッカラーズの最も愛される作品。
books.descriptionEn: Twelve-year-old Frankie Addams is determined to go along with her brother's wedding—to be a member of it, to belong to something at last. One hot summer in a small Southern town, she aches with adolescent loneliness and the longing to become one with someone. McCullers's most beloved novel renders that ache with unbearable accuracy.
books.whyReadEn: No writer has captured the sensation of adolescence so precisely. Short, beautiful, and strange—the tenderest book McCullers ever wrote. It will remind you what it felt like to be twelve, and to wish you were part of something.

books.title: The Glass Palace
books.author: Amitav Ghosh
books.authorJa: アミターヴ・ゴーシュ
books.descriptionJa: 19世紀末ビルマ。少年ラジクールはイギリス軍の侵攻によって亡命し、ラングーン、インド、マラヤへと人生の舞台を移す。東南アジアの近現代史を、一人の男の生涯として描く大河小説。
books.whyReadJa: 東南アジアの歴史を文学として読む。アジア横断的な視点が新鮮。
books.selectionReasonJa: 東南アジア近現代史を一人の男の生涯として描く、ゴーシュの大河。
books.descriptionEn: Burma at the end of the nineteenth century: the boy Rajkumar, orphaned and penniless, watches the British invasion overturn his world. Driven into exile, he moves his life's stage across Rangoon, the forests of India, and Malaya, building a fortune as empires rise and fall. A great family saga that reads the modern history of Southeast Asia through a single man's lifetime.
books.whyReadEn: Southeast Asian history read as literature, with a fresh, cross-Asian perspective that few novelists command. Ambitious, panoramic, and deeply humane—Ghosh at the height of his powers, and a rare window onto the Burma we never see in the news.

books.title: Sea of Poppies
books.titleJa: 海の海に咲くけしの花
books.author: Amitav Ghosh
books.authorJa: アミターヴ・ゴーシュ
books.descriptionJa: アヘン戦争前夜、ビルマと中国を結ぶ「奴隷船イブス号」に乗り合わせた、カーストも言語も異なる人々。ゴーシュ「イビス三部作」の第一作。多言語の世界を描く壮大な海洋小説。
books.whyReadJa: 英語・ヒンディー語・客家語が交錯する、多言語の大河小説。
books.selectionReasonJa: 多言語が交錯する、ゴーシュ「イビス三部作」の海洋大河。
books.descriptionEn: On the eve of the Opium War, a wildly mixed company—castes, languages, and fates thrown together—boards the Ibis, a former slave ship sailing the sea lanes between Burma and China. The first volume of Amitav Ghosh's Ibis Trilogy, it is a magnificent maritime novel of a polyglot world on the brink of upheaval.
books.whyReadEn: A multilingual epic in which English, Hindi, Hindustani, and Hakka mingle and collide—language itself becomes a character. The first panel of a trilogy that grows richer with every volume: adventurous, linguistically dazzling, and enormously fun.

books.title: 雪国
books.author: Kawabata Yasunari
books.descriptionJa: 東京から雪国へ通う島村と、芸者駒子の愛の物語。日本の美意識の精髄を、雪と鏡と虚空のイメージで描いた、川端康成の代表作。ノーベル文学賞の受賞理由となった作品の一つ。
books.whyReadJa: 海外で最も高く評価される日本文学の一つ。日本の「美」を世界に伝えた古典として、外国文学を読む前に一度は手にしたい。
books.selectionReasonJa: 日本人初のノーベル文学賞受賞作家・川端康成の代表作。日本の美意識を世界に知らしめた名作。
books.descriptionEn: Shimamura, a Tokyo dilettante, makes the long train journey into the snow country for a series of brief, passionless visits to Komako, a geisha in a hot-spring town. Kawabata's representative novel renders the essence of Japanese aesthetics through images of snow, mirrors, and emptiness, in prose of almost unbearable delicacy. It was among the works cited when he won the Nobel Prize.
books.whyReadEn: One of the Japanese novels most highly regarded abroad—the book that carried Japan's "beauty" to the world. Read it as a gateway before venturing into foreign literatures: it proves that the most local art can be the most universal.

books.title: 金閣寺
books.titleEn: The Temple of the Golden Pavilion
books.author: Yukio Mishima
books.descriptionJa: 吃音に悩む青年が、美の象徴である金閣寺に執着し、やがて放火に至る。美と自己の関係を哲学的に描いた三島由紀夫の最高傑作。実話に基づく、日本文学の到達点。
books.whyReadJa: 「美とは何か」を問う文学の極致。海外でも最も翻訳される日本文学の一つで、世界文学との対話に開かれた作品。
books.selectionReasonJa: 三島由紀夫の代表作。美と破壊をめぐる哲学的問いで、世界文学史に残る日本文学の古典。
books.descriptionEn: A young acolyte, tormented by a stammer that cuts him off from others, becomes obsessed with the Golden Pavilion in Kyoto—for him the absolute symbol of beauty, and of everything that shuts him out. His obsession finally drives him to burn it down. Mishima's supreme masterwork, a philosophical treatment of beauty and the self, based on a true incident and a summit of Japanese literature.
books.whyReadEn: The extreme of literature that asks "what is beauty?"—and what it costs those who worship it. One of the most translated works of Japanese literature, open to dialogue with world literature, and unsettling in exactly the way great art should be.

books.title: 人間失格
books.author: Osamu Dazai
books.descriptionJa: 「人間として失格」した男・大庭葉蔵の自叙。道化を演じ続け、酒と女に堕ちていく生涯を、太宰治自身の半生と重ねて描く。日本で最も読まれ、世界に翻訳された近代日本文学の金字塔。
books.whyReadJa: 「生きづらさ」をこれほど率直に描いた文学は稀。世界の現代作家（イシグロなど）にも影響を与えた、普遍的な自意識の物語。
books.selectionReasonJa: 太宰治の代表作。日本で最も読まれ、海外翻訳も多い近代日本文学の古典。
books.descriptionEn: The self-narration of Ōba Yōzō, a man "disqualified as human." From childhood he plays the clown to survive, hiding his true self behind a mask of cheerfulness, then sinks into drink, women, and dependence. Dazai overlays the story with his own half-life. The most widely read and most translated monument of modern Japanese literature.
books.whyReadEn: Literature rarely depicts "the pain of living" so candidly. A story of universal self-consciousness that influenced writers worldwide, including Kazuo Ishiguro—and one that speaks directly to every reader who has felt out of step with being human.

books.title: 砂の女
books.author: Kobo Abe
books.descriptionJa: 昆虫採集に出かけた男が、砂の穴に住む女とともに監禁される。毎日砂を掻き出さねば生きられない世界で、男は自由と共同体の意味を問われる。読売文学賞受賞。映画化もされた安部公房の代表作。
books.whyReadJa: 「自由とは何か」をSF的に問う、世界に評価された日本文学。カフカの系譜を日本で継承した異色作。
books.selectionReasonJa: 安部公房の代表作。世界SF文学の最高峰に位置づけられ、日本文学の国際化を先導した。
books.descriptionEn: A schoolteacher out collecting insects is lured into a house at the bottom of a deep sand pit, inhabited by a woman who is the village's prisoner. He is trapped. In a world where survival means shoveling sand every day, he is forced to reconsider freedom, labor, and community. Winner of the Yomiuri Prize and filmed by Hiroshi Teshigahara, this is Kōbō Abe's representative novel.
books.whyReadEn: A world-renowned work of Japanese literature that asks "what is freedom?" in a science-fictional key—an eccentric masterpiece that carries Kafka's lineage into Japan and asks questions that refuse easy answers.

books.title: 蛙
books.author: Mo Yan
books.descriptionJa: 産児制限政策を執行する村の助産師ガーヌー。彼女の人生を通して、中国の人口政策と個人の苦悩を描く。ノーベル文学賞受賞作家・莫言の、最も社会性の強い傑作。
books.whyReadJa: 中国現代史を一人の女性の人生から描く、ノーベル賞作家の代表作。中国社会を深く理解する入口。
books.selectionReasonJa: ノーベル文学賞受賞作家・莫言の代表作。中国現代史を文学化した金字塔。
books.descriptionEn: Gugu, a village midwife, is charged with enforcing China's family-planning policy—a role that makes her both savior and executioner in her community. Through her long life, Mo Yan portrays the policy's enormous human cost and the anguish of individuals caught inside it. The most socially engaged masterwork of the Nobel laureate.
books.whyReadEn: A Nobel laureate's representative novel, drawing China's modern history through one woman's life. An honest, painful entrance into understanding contemporary Chinese society—and a book that examines a national policy with real moral seriousness.

books.title: 活着
books.author: Yu Hua
books.descriptionJa: 大地主の息子フーグイは、賭博で財産を失い、家族とともに中国の激動の時代を生き抜く。文化大革命を経て、最期に残るものとは。映画化（張芸謀監督）でも知られる、中国現代文学の名作。
books.whyReadJa: 「生きる」ことの意味を、中国の苦難の歴史の中で描く。世界で最も読まれる中国小説の一つ。
books.selectionReasonJa: 余華の代表作。中国現代文学を代表し、世界で広く読まれる名作。
books.descriptionEn: Fugui, the spoiled son of a great landowner, gambles away his family's fortune and must survive the great upheavals of twentieth-century China alongside his wife and children—war, land reform, famine, and the Cultural Revolution. What remains, when almost everything is taken? A classic of contemporary Chinese literature, also known through Zhang Yimou's celebrated film.
books.whyReadEn: The meaning of "living"—of going on—set against China's suffering history. One of the most widely read Chinese novels in the world, and the quickest way to feel a century of Chinese life from the inside.

books.title: 엄마를 부탁해
books.titleJa: お母さんを尋ねて三千里
books.author: Shin Kyung-sook
books.descriptionJa: ソウルの地下鉄で母が行方不明になった。家族四人の視点から、母の人生と、知らなかった母の顔が浮かび上がる。韓国で200万部、世界30か国で翻訳された、韓国文学を世界に知らしめた代表作。
books.whyReadJa: 「母」と「家族」をめぐる最も普遍的な物語。韓国文学の国際的な知名度を高めた、ブックスタート的な一冊。
books.selectionReasonJa: シン・ギョンスクの代表作。韓国文学の国際化を牽引した、世界で最も読まれた韓国小説。
books.descriptionEn: A mother, sixty-nine years old, vanishes on the Seoul subway—walked ahead of her husband, lost, and never found. Told through the voices of her four children and husband, the story slowly surfaces her life, and the face of the mother they never really knew. With two million copies sold in Korea and translations in thirty countries, this is the work that made Korean literature known to the world.
books.whyReadEn: The most universal story about "mother" and "family"—the book that raised Korean literature's international profile and made Shin Kyung-sook a name read worldwide. A place to begin, and a door that opens onto an entire literature.

books.title: סיפור על אהבה וחושך
books.titleEn: A Tale of Love and Darkness
books.author: Amos Oz
books.descriptionJa: エルサレムのユダヤ人家庭で育った少年の記憶。イスラエル建国前夜の時代と家族を、イスラエルを代表する作家アモス・オズが壮大に描く自伝的小説。世界文学の傑作。
books.whyReadJa: イスラエルと中東の現実を、ひとりの少年の物語として体験できる。パレスチナ問題を文学から考える入口。
books.selectionReasonJa: イスラエルを代表する作家アモス・オズの代表作。中東文学の金字塔。
books.descriptionEn: The memories of a boy raised in a small Jerusalem apartment in the 1940s, among books and storytellers, on the eve of Israel's founding. Israel's foremost writer, Amos Oz, renders with epic sweep the era and his own family—its love, its silences, and its tragedy. A masterpiece of world literature, and an essential portrait of a nation coming into being.
books.whyReadEn: Experience the reality of Israel and the Middle East as one boy's story—a literary gateway into thinking about the Palestinian question with the complexity it deserves, and into the mind of one of the region's greatest writers.

books.title: أولاد حارتنا
books.author: Naguib Mahfouz
books.authorJa: ナギーブ・マフフーズ
books.descriptionJa: カイロの路地を舞台に、四世代にわたる英雄たちの物語を寓話として描く。預言者たちの物語を想起させる構図で、宗教と社会を問う。ノーベル文学賞受賞作家マフフーズの最高傑作。
books.whyReadJa: アラブ文学の最高峰。ノーベル賞を受賞したマフフーズが、宗教と人間を寓話として描いた金字塔。
books.selectionReasonJa: アラブ世界初のノーベル文学賞作家マフフーズの代表作。アラブ文学の金字塔。
books.descriptionEn: Set in a single Cairo alley, this allegory unfolds the stories of its heroes across four generations—each echoing the lives of the prophets. Through them Mahfouz interrogates religion, faith, and society with a boldness that scandalized and thrilled readers. The supreme masterwork of the Nobel laureate, and one of the most controversial books of the Arab world.
books.whyReadEn: The summit of Arabic literature—Mahfouz's Nobel-winning allegory of religion and humanity, told through the story of one street and the people who walk it. Daring when it appeared, and still capable of provoking and rewarding.

books.title: Disgrace
books.author: J.M. Coetzee
books.descriptionJa: 大学講師デイヴィッド・ルーリーは、スキャンダルで職を追われ、娘の農場に身を寄せる。そこで起きた暴力的事件を機に、南アフリカの「恥辱」の歴史と向き合う。ブッカー賞2度受賞、ノーベル賞作家クッツェーの代表作。
books.whyReadJa: アパルトヘイト後の南アフリカと、人間の尊厳を問う、ノーベル賞作家の最高傑作。
books.selectionReasonJa: ノーベル文学賞・ブッカー賞受賞作家クッツェーの代表作。南アフリカ文学の金字塔。
books.descriptionEn: David Lurie, a twice-divorced professor in Cape Town, loses his position after an affair with a student and takes refuge at his daughter's small farm in the countryside. A violent attack there forces him to confront the meaning of "disgrace"—his own, his daughter's, and his country's. The representative novel of J.M. Coetzee, twice a Booker winner and a Nobel laureate.
books.whyReadEn: Post-apartheid South Africa and the question of human dignity, interrogated with an almost unbearable spareness. The Nobel laureate's greatest novel—and one of the definitive books of our era, with nothing extraneous in it.

books.title: The Famished Road
books.author: Ben Okri
books.descriptionJa: 生と死の間を彷徨う「アビク」の少年アザロが、ナイジェリアの路地で見る現実と精霊の世界。マジックリアリズムとアフリカの口承文芸が融合し、ブッカー賞を受賞した、アフリカ文学の金字塔。
books.whyReadJa: アフリカのマジックリアリズムの到達点。ブッカー賞受賞作として、アフリカ文学の国際化を担った。
books.selectionReasonJa: ブッカー賞受賞のベン・オクリ代表作。アフリカ文学の国際的な金字塔。
books.descriptionEn: Azaro, an "abiku"—a spirit-child who hovers between the world of the dead and the world of the living—grows up on a crowded, decaying street in an unnamed Nigerian city. He sees both the brutal realities of poverty and the shimmering spirit world all around. Fusing magical realism with African oral tradition, this Booker Prize winner is a monument of African literature.
books.whyReadEn: The summit of African magical realism, where the spirit world and the political street are one. As a Booker winner, it carried African literature onto the international stage—and its voice remains unlike anything else.

books.title: Rayuela
books.author: Julio Cortázar
books.descriptionJa: パリとブエノスアイレスを舞台に、オラシオとラ・マガの愛と精神の探求を描く。読む順番を自由に選べる「読者への提案」を付した、ラテンアメリカ文学の実験的傑作。
books.whyReadJa: 「読む」ことの可能性を拡張した、ラテンアメリカ文学の最重要作。ガルシア＝マルケスと並ぶ「ブーム」の旗手。
books.selectionReasonJa: ラテンアメリカ文学ブームを代表するコルタサルの最高傑作。
books.descriptionEn: Set between Paris and Buenos Aires, it follows Horacio Oliveira and La Maga in their restless search for love, art, and a meaning strong enough to hold them. Furnished with a "table of instructions" that lets readers choose the order of chapters—and even to skip the "expendable" ones—it is the experimental masterwork of Latin American literature.
books.whyReadEn: The work that expanded the very possibilities of "reading"—you help build the novel as you go. A central text of the Latin American Boom, standing beside García Márquez, and one of the great love stories of the century.

books.title: La muerte de Artemio Cruz
books.titleJa: アルテミオ・クルスの死
books.author: Carlos Fuentes
books.authorJa: カルロス・フエンテス
books.descriptionJa: 瀕死の富豪アルテミオ・クルスの過去と現在が、意識の流れで交錯する。メキシコ革命から現代に至る国家の歴史を、一人の男の人生として描く、メキシコ文学の金字塔。
books.whyReadJa: メキシコ現代史を文学として読む。ラテンアメリカ文学ブームのもう一つの柱、フエンテスの代表作。
books.selectionReasonJa: メキシコを代表する作家フエンテスの代表作。ラテンアメリカ文学の金字塔。
books.descriptionEn: Artemio Cruz, a corrupt tycoon, lies dying; his past and present interweave in a relentless stream of consciousness, told in three voices—I, you, he. From the Mexican Revolution to the modern era, the history of the nation is rendered as the life of a single man, with all its betrayal and hunger. A monument of Mexican literature.
books.whyReadEn: Read Mexico's modern history as literature—the representative novel of Fuentes, another pillar of the Latin American Boom, and a savage, brilliant reckoning with the bargain between revolution and power.

books.title: A Case of Exploding Mangoes
books.titleJa: 爆発するマンゴーの事件
books.author: Mohammed Hanif
books.descriptionJa: 1988年に墜落死したパキスタンのジア大統領。その謎の死を、黒いユーモアと風刺で描く政治小説。ブッカー賞最終候補。パキスタン文学を世界に知らしめた、痛快な傑作。
books.whyReadJa: 政治と笑いを融合させた、現代パキスタン文学の代表作。南アジアの文学の新しい波。
books.selectionReasonJa: ブッカー賞最終候補となった、パキスタン文学の世界的代表作。
books.descriptionEn: President Zia-ul-Haq of Pakistan died in a mysterious plane crash in 1988—along with, supposedly, his American ambassador and a case of mangoes. This political novel takes that death as material for black humor, satire, and conspiracy in equal measure. A Booker Prize finalist, and a rollicking, wicked masterwork that introduced Pakistani literature to the world.
books.whyReadEn: The representative novel of contemporary Pakistani literature, fusing politics and laughter with a lightness that conceals real anger. Part of South Asia's new wave—and one of the most fun serious novels you will ever read.

books.title: The Gangster We Are All Looking For
books.titleEn: The Gangster We Are All Looking For
books.titleJa: 私たちが探しているギャング
books.author: lê thi diem thúy
books.authorJa: レ・ティ・ディエム・トゥイ
books.descriptionJa: ベトナム戦争後にアメリカへ亡命した家族の、断片的な記憶。海、父の暴力、母の沈黙——ベトナム系アメリカ文学の、抒情的な傑作。
books.whyReadJa: ベトナム戦争の「その後」を、難民の視点から描く。オーシャン・ヴオンやウェンと繋がる、ベトナム系文学の源流。
books.selectionReasonJa: ベトナム系アメリカ文学を代表する、抒情的な傑作。
books.descriptionEn: Fragmented, luminous memories of a Vietnamese family who fled the war and resettled in America—the sea crossing, a father's violence, a mother's silence, a little girl learning a new language and a new self. Written in a voice at once spare and lyrical, it is a masterwork of Vietnamese American literature.
books.whyReadEn: The "aftermath" of the Vietnam War seen from a refugee's perspective—the source spring of Vietnamese American literature, flowing toward Ocean Vuong and beyond. Short, intense, and unforgettable; its fragments cohere into a single song.

books.title: Changes
books.author: Ama Ata Aidoo
books.authorJa: アマ・アタ・アイドゥー
books.descriptionJa: ガーナのキャリア女性エシが、夫の浮気に傷つき、結婚と恋愛の自由を求める。アフリカの女性解放と伝統の葛藤を描く、アフリカ女性文学の古典。
books.whyReadJa: アフリカの「女性」を中心に据えた文学の古典。世界文学としてのアフリカ女性の声を知る。
books.selectionReasonJa: ガーナを代表する女性作家アイドゥーの代表作。アフリカ女性文学の古典。
books.descriptionEn: Esi, a successful career woman in Accra, is wounded by her husband's infidelity and leaves him—only to find that the freedom she wins brings its own complications in a Ghanaian society still bound by tradition. A classic of African women's literature, depicting the conflict between women's liberation and the weight of custom with wit and honesty.
books.whyReadEn: A classic that places African "women" at the center of the literary stage—the voice of African womanhood speaking to world literature, and an early landmark in the conversation that continues today.

books.title: Cantik Itu Luka
books.author: Eka Kurniawan
books.descriptionJa: 第二次世界大戦後のインドネシアを舞台に、不死身の美女デウィ・アユの数奇な運命を描く。暴力と笑いとファンタジーが交錯する、東南アジア文学の新たな金字塔。
books.whyReadJa: 「東南アジアのマルケス」と呼ばれるクルニアワンの代表作。東南アジア文学の国際的な顔。
books.selectionReasonJa: インドネシア文学を国際的に知らしめた、エカ・クルニアワンの代表作。
books.descriptionEn: Set in Indonesia after the Second World War, it follows the extraordinary fate of Dewi Ayu, an immortal beauty who dies and returns, and of her daughters, each cursed in her own way. Violence, laughter, and fantasy collide in a story that spans decades of Indonesian history—a new monument of Southeast Asian literature, and the book that made Kurniawan famous.
books.whyReadEn: The representative novel of Eka Kurniawan, called "Southeast Asia's García Márquez"—the international face of Southeast Asian literature. Wild, dark, and hilarious; read it and you'll see why the comparison fits.

books.title: The Luminaries
books.author: Eleanor Catton
books.descriptionJa: 1866年、ニュージーランドの金鉱街で起きた失踪と死の謎。12人の登場人物が、星座の配置に従って織りなすヴィクトリア朝風の大長編。ブッカー賞を史上最年少で受賞した、超弩級の傑作。
books.whyReadJa: オセアニア文学の到達点。星座の構造で紡がれる、800ページの驚異的なミステリ。
books.selectionReasonJa: ブッカー賞最年少受賞となった、ニュージーランド文学の金字塔。
books.descriptionEn: In 1866, in a New Zealand gold-rush town, a man vanishes and another is found dead—just as twelve men gather in a candlelit room to share their stories. Each is a sign of the zodiac, and the novel's structure follows the positions of the stars. Winner of the Booker Prize at the youngest age in its history—a colossal, breathtaking masterwork.
books.whyReadEn: The summit of Oceanian literature—an astonishing 800-page mystery whose structure is governed by the constellations. Ambitious, intricate, and deeply entertaining; a triumph of architecture in fiction and of sheer storytelling nerve.

books.title: 紅楼夢
books.author: Cao Xueqin
books.descriptionJa: 清朝の名門・賈家の栄華と没落を、通霊宝玉の化身とされる宝玉と二人の女性の悲恋を軸に描く、中国文学最大の長編小説。百二十回にも及ぶ人間群像の細密描写は、中国四大奇書・四大名著の頂点に立つ。未完のまま著者を失いながらも、中国の国民的古典として読み継がれる。
books.whyReadJa: 中国文学の最高峰にして国民的古典。名門一族の栄華と没落を描く、世界有数の大河小説。
books.selectionReasonJa: 中国文学の金字塔。四大名著の頂点として、日本の文学や文化を理解する上でも欠かせない一冊。
books.descriptionEn: The glory and decline of the great Qing dynasty house of Jia, told through the love of Bao-yu, the incarnation of a sacred stone, and the two women of the house, Baochai and Dai-yu. With a cast of hundreds drawn in meticulous detail across 120 chapters, this is the summit of Chinese literature and of the Four Great Classical Novels. Left unfinished at the author's death, it endures as China's national classic—a family saga, a love story, and a meditation on impermanence.
books.whyReadEn: The summit of Chinese literature and a national classic. A sweeping saga of a great family's glory and fall—essential for understanding Chinese literature and the culture that shaped it for centuries.

books.title: 源氏物語
books.author: Murasaki Shikibu
books.descriptionJa: 平安時代の光源氏の恋と栄華、その没落後の世界までを描く、世界最古の長編小説とされる紫式部の大作。約五十四帖、登場人物数百人の王朝ロマンスは、恋の機微から人間の業、無常観までを精緻に描く。千年を経てなお世界文学の最高峰として称賛され続ける、日本文学の原点。
books.whyReadJa: 世界最古の長編小説にして日本文学の原点。千年読み継がれる繊細な心理描写は、いまなお読者の心を揺さぶる。
books.selectionReasonJa: 日本文学の原点にして世界最古の長編小説。千年を超えて世界文学の最高峰に立ち続ける一冊。
books.descriptionEn: The love and glory of the shining Genji, the courtly romance of the Heian era, extends to the world after his decline. In roughly fifty-four chapters and a cast of hundreds, Murasaki Shikibu's great work—often called the world's first novel—renders with exquisite precision the subtleties of love, human karma, and the Buddhist sense of impermanence. A thousand years on, it is still praised as one of the summits of world literature and the origin of the Japanese novel.
books.whyReadEn: The world's first novel and the very origin of Japanese literature. Its delicate psychological portraiture, read for a thousand years, still moves the modern heart just as it always has.
